objective: Close the authenticated nonsecret sidecar control and ROM bridge seam for regional presence.
decisions: Keep GAME_PROTOCOL_VERSION and the fixed bridge ABI at version 1; the five presence bridge message IDs already exist.
Bump only CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION from 1 to 2 so new launchers fail the handshake against old sidecars before exchanging new variants.
Reuse strict coop-protocol LocalPresenceStateV1, PresenceInteractionV1, RemotePlayerSpawnV1, RemotePlayerUpdateV1, and RemotePlayerDespawnV1 types directly.
Add remote_player_spawn, remote_player_update, and remote_player_despawn ControlCommand variants from launcher to sidecar.
Add player_state and interact_remote_player ControlEvent variants from sidecar to launcher.
Do not include session_epoch in presence messages because the authenticated control connection is already epoch-bound.
Never transfer endpoint, bearer ticket, access or refresh token, runtime fence, PresenceReady, or build identity across local IPC.
Decode and validate exact ROM payloads before committing the incoming outer sequence; commit before the best-effort control-event write to avoid replaying an ambiguous interaction.
Preserve embedded cloud server_sequence values and allocate independent sidecar-owned outer bridge sequences for every lifecycle frame.
Transient presence bypasses command_history, deferred_commands, checkpoint replay, and routine command capacity.
Reject launcher-origin presence before ROM readiness and during quiescing; never defer presence across a bridge generation.

On same-socket ROM reboot, SESSION_READY remains first and queued presence is not replayed. Launcher integration must cancel the current realtime core and mint a fresh ticket after the generation reset.
implementation_requirements: Keep the existing loopback-only three-second authenticated handshake and bounded sixteen-candidate acceptance behavior.
Keep the control reader and bridge reader single-owner tasks and capacity-one channels; LocalSidecar remains the sole ControlWriter and BridgeWriter owner.
PlayerState and Interaction frames require current epoch and acknowledged ROM readiness.
Malformed presence payloads produce a fixed protocol violation without advancing last_session_rom.
Valid stale outer frames may be ignored through existing serial-order inspection without mutating presence.
Allocate no presence bridge sequence and perform no presence write once quiescing begins.
Retain current biased shutdown/deadline priority and clean EOF behavior.
Update exhaustive launcher matches in the later launcher integration unit; do not weaken local message strictness to ease integration.
required_tests: Strict canonical round trips, unknown-field rejection, invalid values, and sub-512-byte lines for all five control variants.
Control protocol incompatibility uses CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION + 1 rather than a hard-coded value.
Bidirectional relay preserves exact inner payloads, current epoch, and independent outer bridge sequences.
Malformed 28-byte and 20-byte payload cases prove no ROM sequence commit and no control event.
Presence variants never enter command_history or deferred_commands.
Quiescing produces no presence bridge write or sequence allocation.
Pre-bridge presence flood leaves shutdown reservation usable.
Reboot ordering proves SESSION_READY precedes fresh presence.
Fragmented/interleaved bridge-control coverage accounts for the newly emitted PlayerState event.
known_integration_risks: The current launcher ControlChannel is synchronously borrowed; the end-to-end launcher unit needs a continuously draining bounded I/O owner so 10 Hz presence cannot consume checkpoint timing.
A same-socket ROM reboot resets inner source and warp sequences; continuing the existing realtime connection would make the cloud ignore regressed local state and can strand cleared remote reducers.
A single TCP stream cannot overtake transient JSON already written, so launcher output coalescing and critical-write priority remain necessary.
